findings.text: Provides an integer vector sysctl handler that forwards to a shared vector routine configured for signed integers with the standard integer conversion.
Alternative build of the integer vector handler that is unavailable and reports operation not implemented without touching caller buffers.
Alternative build of the bounded integer vector handler that is unavailable and reports operation not implemented.
Exposes three mutable global IPC sizing values for maximum identifier count, its shift, and its minimum cycle that other IPC code reads and that a boot option can widen.
Provides per-namespace lifecycle operations that install a private copy of the IPC sysctl table on namespace setup and unregister plus release it on teardown, reporting failure if registration fails.
Provides per-namespace lifecycle operations that install a private copy of the message queue sysctl table under the mqueue path on setup and unregister plus release it on teardown.
Exposes helpers that translate a namespace-local user or group identifier toward the global space through a single-element downward mapping, plus the single-element downward mapper itself.
Exposes a membership test for the effective group plus supplementary list and a binary search over the supplementary group array.
Vector handlers produce an empty result and success when the table has no data, declares no length, is called with no length, or is read from a nonzero file position.
Unsigned integer vectors accept only a single element; a table sized for more is rejected as invalid.

Writes are bounded to one page minus one byte, leading blanks are skipped before every value, trailing blanks are skipped after the last value, and a write that yields no values is rejected as invalid.

A negative sign on an unsigned vector element is rejected, values are dispatched through a per-type converter in both directions, read output separates elements with tabs and terminates a nonempty successful read with a newline when space remains, and the file position advances by bytes consumed or produced.
A write starting at nonzero offset is ignored under strict handling, warns once but proceeds under warning handling, and proceeds silently otherwise.

Inbound integer tokens allow one leading minus, require at least one digit, use lenient base detection, reject overflow and overlong tokens that fill the scratch buffer, and require the following character to belong to an allowed separator set when such a set is supplied.
Lenient string conversion normalizes the radix, parses the widest unsigned form, and reports range error when the value overflows that form or does not fit in an unsigned long.
Numeric and character output helpers never write past the supplied remaining length and update both the cursor and the remaining count for what was actually stored.
The semaphore vector handler snapshots the fourth control value, delegates to the generic integer vector handler, validates the new fourth value, and restores the snapshot when either step fails.
The fourth semaphore control value is valid only from zero up to the current global maximum identifier count inclusive; anything outside yields a range error.
The automatic message queue identifier control uses a dummy integer, logs a one-time notice that writes have no effect, and then behaves like a bounded integer vector on that dummy.

The IPC sysctl table publishes shared memory, message, semaphore and optional checkpoint identifier controls backed by initial namespace fields, mostly readable and writable by owner with world read, while the next identifier controls are read only and the automatic control has no backing store.
Message queue controls bound maximum and default message count and size between global minima and hard maxima, while the queue count has no explicit bounds.

Namespace setup duplicates the template table and rewrites each entry that pointed at the initial namespace to point at the new namespace counterpart, clearing any other entry to no backing store before registration.

Downward identifier mapping issues a read barrier, selects a linear scan for small extent counts and a binary search for large counts, requires the whole requested range to lie inside one extent, and yields all bits set when no extent matches.
Supplementary group lookup treats a missing list as absent and otherwise performs a binary search over an ordered group array, returning found only on exact equality.
Effective group membership is true when the queried group equals the current effective group or appears in the supplementary list.

IPC and message queue permission checks start from the table mode, shift it for owner or group match against the owning namespace root identities, keep only the low three bits, then replicate those bits to owner group and other.

When checkpoint support is present, the next identifier controls become widely writable for a caller with namespace checkpoint capability without audit; otherwise they follow the normal owner and group derivation.
Table ownership is the mapped namespace root user and group when those mappings are valid and otherwise falls back to the global root identities.
Lookup resolves to the sysctl set of the current task IPC namespace and the visibility test reports true only for that same set.
Acquiring a namespace reference from an mqueue inode is serialized by taking the global mqueue lock around the lookup and releasing it immediately after.
Filesystem context for mqueue carries a pointer to the associated IPC namespace and a flag recording whether that namespace was newly created.
Priority tree node for queued messages links into a balanced tree, anchors a list of messages at one priority, and stores that priority value.
Extended waiter records the sleeping task, list linkage, an optional loaded message pointer, and a state that distinguishes empty from ready.

Queue inode state holds a spinlock, embedded VFS inode, wait queue, message priority tree with rightmost and cached node hints, queue attributes, notification event with owner, execution identity, user namespace, accounting, socket and cookie, two waiter slots for senders and receivers, and total in-memory queue size.
Queue inodes are allocated from a dedicated slab cache and the container helper recovers the queue state from the embedded VFS inode.

Vector transfer operates in two directions: inbound parses whitespace separated tokens into kernel slots through converters, outbound formats kernel slots into tab separated text with trailing newline; both share element count and error short-circuiting.
Extended waiters move between empty and ready, with separate slots reserving one side for senders waiting for space and the other for receivers waiting for messages.
Integer, semaphore and automatic message queue handlers serve as sysctl dispatch targets receiving table, direction, buffer, length and position.
Per-namespace sysctl roots expose lookup, permission and ownership callbacks that bind tables to the current IPC namespace and derive access from its root identities.
Boot initialization registers the initial IPC sysctl table and warns on failure, while a dedicated boot option widens the global identifier limits and logs the new maximum.
Overlong numeric input is rejected rather than truncated, output silently truncates when the caller buffer fills, and writes longer than a page are silently capped before parsing.
Writes starting at nonzero offsets currently warn in permissive modes but are documented as future failures, so callers depending on them risk breakage when strict handling becomes mandatory.
Mqueue filesystem identity and name sizing facts: magic number 0x19800202, directory entry size 20, file name size 80.
Waiter direction and state encodings: send zero, receive one, empty zero, ready one, with two waiter slots indexed by direction.
Tunable controls carry mode 0644, next identifier controls carry 0444 normally and 0666 for privileged checkpoint callers.
